# `hs-run git` — state map

<!-- generated by render_state_map.py — edit the SSOT, # learn: "${HARNESS_BIN_ROOT:-.}"/harness/data/hs-run-registry.d/<domain>.yaml, not this file -->

Every state `hs-run git` can report, with what it means. Run the CLI, read the `state`, do the judgment that state names, run it again — each state is re-derived from artifacts on disk, so deleting an artifact regresses the state.

This file is generated. Change the source named in the comment above, then re-render with `render_state_map.py`; edits made here are lost on the next render.

## States that route something

The CLI hands these rule and reference paths over at the moment the step begins — the body does not repeat them.

| state | what it means | routes |
|---|---|---|
| `sequencer_in_progress` | Git is mid-operation and staging the conflict fix silenced the conflict check without ending it. What to do next differs by operation, and the envelope says which: mid-merge, cherry-pick or revert the commit is what CONCLUDES the operation, so it is the right move (rung 10). Mid-rebase HEAD is detached, a commit finishes only the current step, and `git rebase --abort` discards it — so that one stops (rung 2). | `verification-mechanism` |
| `secret_found` | The staged diff carries something that looks like a credential. Stop. Do not commit it "to fix later" — a secret in a commit is in the history whether or not the next commit removes it. | `references/safety-protocols.md` |
| `ready` | The staged diff is clean and split into commits. The verb computed the split; it did not choose the messages or the grouping — that is this step's judgment, and the two drawers here are what it is judged against. | `references/workflow-commit.md`, `references/commit-standards.md` |
| `no_upstream` | This branch tracks nothing. A first push needs `-u` to set the upstream, which is a different command from the one every later push uses. | `references/workflow-push.md` |
| `no_plan_resolved` | The same push gate refuses, but for the one reason no receipt can fix: with no plan resolved there is nowhere for a receipt to live. Open a plan under plans/ with `status: in_progress`, or point HARNESS_ACTIVE_PLAN at one. `ship` rules the identical tree the same way at the same rung. | `verification-mechanism` |
| `push_gate_blocked` | The push would go through locally — the pre-push hook only warns on a receipt gap — but CI's receipts-gate enforces it. The reason is in the envelope, and the call on whether to push anyway is the model's. | `verification-mechanism` |
| `ready_to_push` | HEAD is ahead of its upstream and the pre-push gate passes. The commits are in the envelope; the drawer covers the failure modes a push still has after that. | `references/workflow-push.md` |

## States that route nothing

Not a gap: each is fully served by the `next_action` line the envelope already carries, and needs no extra file to act on.

| state | what it means |
|---|---|
| `help` | Usage was asked for. Nothing was read and nothing was decided. |
| `git_diff_failed` | git itself failed on a real repository. Not "nothing staged": an empty answer from a broken git would read as a clean tree and skip the secret scan. |
| `nothing_staged` | Nothing is staged, so there is nothing to plan. Stage what belongs in this commit first; the verb reads the index, never the working tree. |
| `unresolved_conflict` | The index has unmerged paths. `git commit` refuses to run on it, and so does this — resolve the conflict, stage the resolution, then ask again. |
| `nothing_to_push` | HEAD is not ahead of its upstream. Nothing to push — and if that is a surprise, the commits went somewhere other than this branch. |
